about.statement: I'm a product designer who cares about the details, from how a product works to how it feels.
about.paragraph: I help brands, startups, and teams turn ideas into clear, usable digital products. My work covers the full journey: understanding users, shaping the experience, designing the interface, and building interactive websites that bring it all to life. I use AI-assisted development to move from concept to live product quickly, without losing attention to craft.

process.heading: A clear process, from first idea to final launch.
process.intro: Every project follows a simple, transparent path, so you always know what's happening and what comes next.

steps.title: Discover
steps.text: I start by understanding your goals, your users, and the problem we're solving through conversations, research, and a close look at what already exists.

steps.title: Define
steps.text: I turn insights into structure by mapping user flows, organizing content, and sketching wireframes so we agree on direction before visual design begins.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: I craft the interface with care: clean layouts, consistent components, and thoughtful details, then refine it with your feedback.

steps.title: Develop & Launch
steps.text: I build the design into a fast, responsive, interactive website, test it across devices, and launch it, with support after it goes live.

projects.summary: A luxury e-commerce experience for hand-embroidered Hyderabadi heritage wear, with an interactive fitting canvas for made-to-measure orders.
projects.overview: OYE is a bespoke fashion label built around ancestral zardozi embroidery, where every piece is drawn, framed, and stitched by hand by karigars. I designed and built its website to feel like stepping into an atelier: rich, unhurried, and personal, while still working as a smooth online store.
projects.challenge: Luxury handcraft is hard to sell online. Shoppers can't touch the fabric or meet the artisan, and standard S/M/L sizing goes against the idea of made-to-measure clothing. The site needed to tell the craft story, present collections beautifully, and make custom sizing simple enough to do at home.
projects.approach: I built the experience around three ideas: tell the craft story, show the pieces like an exhibition, and turn measuring into a guided, interactive step instead of a form.

features.title: Editorial Hero
features.text: Large "Timeless Grace" typography framing a model cutout, with a slide carousel, pill menu, wishlist, and cart.

features.title: Heritage Storytelling
features.text: Artisan photography paired with the brand story, a signature quote, and key facts.

features.title: Curated Collections
features.text: Women's and Men's collections in arched frames with oversized background words for an exhibition feel.

features.title: Custom Tailoring Studio
features.text: A three-step explanation of made-to-measure: skip standard sizes, learn how to measure, save once for every order.

features.title: Interactive Fitting Canvas
features.text: Shoppers tap points on a mannequin (shoulder, chest, waist, hip, full length) to see exactly where to measure.

features.title: Saved Measurements
features.text: Profiles are stored in the browser, offered again at checkout, and can be switched on or off per order.

designSystem.notes: Arched frames, wide letter-spaced labels, textile-inspired zigzag dividers, and generous spacing create a calm, premium, heritage feel.
